svg.title: From Federal Dollar to Sealed Complaint
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-fca-relator-filing-sequence; chapter number: 1; chart type: process_flow; title: From Federal Dollar to Sealed Complaint; subtitle: Five moves practitioners use to preserve original-source status and relator share; caption: Relators who win pair a material defect with insider documents, serve the written disclosure before filing, and plead the full 10-year window under a seal that runs 60 days on paper and about 2.5 years in practice.; assumptions note: Step order follows the operator gates and pro-tips quoted by the cited practitioners; seal length, the 11-month intervention average, the 10-year window, and the 29 states plus DC figure are reported practitioner claims, not independently verified.; note: Sources: Justia (Hamilton and Newman, HocnawRgrAA), Beverly Hills Bar Association (Mark Kleiman, yN7NRjwYKFs), Phillips & Cohen LLP (5-ptDaAQkvI), Shipman Wright Law (7-9Z8vNWVFc), Brown, LLC (3ugChIElhkM).; stages: step: 01; label: Materiality check; value: Step 1; detail: Confirm the defect is one the payer would refuse to pay for, like out-of-spec military parts rather than wrong-color parts (Justia, Hamilton and Newman).; step: 02; label: Photograph the documents; value: Step 2; detail: Take pictures of documents instead of walking out with them, and audit your own involvement first because dirty hands cut the award (Kleiman; Brown, LLC).; step: 03; label: Serve written disclosure; value: Step 3; detail: Serve the written disclosure statement with all material evidence before filing the complaint (Phillips & Cohen LLP).; step: 04; label: File the sealed complaint; value: Step 4; detail: Plead the full 10-year limitations window plus parallel state counts; 29 states plus DC have FCAs (Justia; Beverly Hills Bar Association).; step: 05; label: Hold the seal in silence; value: Step 5; detail: No media contact while DOJ averages about 11 months to decide intervention; public information disqualifies a relator (Phillips & Cohen; Shipman Wright Law).
